sentence: This project studies how the bacteria Streptococcus pneumoniae cause disease after they colonize the upper respiratory tract.
This project builds computational imaging methods that predict how gastric cancer responds to treatment and how the disease is likely to go.
This project studies how to shorten the gap between discovery and applying evidence-based interventions in community and clinical settings for cancer control.
This project studies how aggregated proteins and dysregulated RNAs take part in genetic neurodegenerative diseases.
This project tests thousands of chemicals for toxicity and looks for the biological networks they change, to help predict which chemicals are toxic.
This project uses patient cells to study how leukemia stem cells and specific mutations start and maintain human acute myeloid leukemia.
This project looks at how artificial intelligence and data from the electronic health record can help identify and treat sepsis.
This project studies how two mismatch repair proteins control a DNA repair pathway called homologous recombination and keep the genome stable.
This project builds a molecular map of all cell types in a brain stem cell reservoir to learn how immune cells affect new neurons.
This project studies the molecular and cellular basis of complex behaviors and of maladaptive behavior related to major psychiatric illnesses.
This project develops and tests a mobile app that uses ecological momentary assessment to collect dietary data with little burden.
This project uses imaging over time and postmortem histopathology to test whether toxic tau spreads along white matter axons in Alzheimer's disease.
This project tests whether acupuncture in the clinic before treatment eases urinary symptoms in people with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
This project develops multi-modal foundation models for the early detection of sepsis that learn from a vast dataset of patient records.
This project develops a method that links a unique RNA barcode to each protein variant so many variants can be tested together in activity assays.
This project studies how respiratory viruses fuse their membrane with host cells to enter them, using biophysical and biochemical tools.
This project tests whether CRISPR gene editing with chemically ligated guide RNA can remove hepatitis B virus DNA that current drugs cannot eliminate.
This project studies how a protein often mutated in neurodevelopmental disorders and cancers regulates genome organization and what mutations do to it.
This project uses a survey to describe who uses cannabidiol products, how they use them with other medications, and what adverse events they report.
This project tries to find out why lung cancer risk from cigarette smoking differs among population groups.
